title: The producer: batching, retries and idempotence
summary: How a record travels from ProduceAsync to the leader, what linger.ms, batch.size and compression buy you, and how the idempotent producer stops retries from writing duplicates.

steps.title: From ProduceAsync to the leader
body: A producer does not send one network request per record. It **batches** per partition:
```text
ProduceAsync(key, value)
v
serializer -> partitioner -> accumulator: one open batch per partition
P0 [r r r r . . ]   <- sent when full (batch.size) ...
P1 [r . . . . . ]   <- ... or when linger.ms has passed
v   background sender (librdkafka threads)
ProduceRequest to each partition's leader
(up to max.in.flight requests per connection)
v
leader + ISR write it (acks=all) -> DeliveryResult { Partition, Offset }
| Setting | Default | Why you change it |
| `linger.ms` | 5 ms (librdkafka; the Java client since Kafka 4.0, it was 0) | wait a little longer (10-50 ms) for fuller batches: higher throughput, a few ms more latency |
| `batch.size` | 16 KiB (Java) / 1 MB (librdkafka, plus `batch.num.messages` 10000) | bigger batches for high-volume topics |
| `compression.type` | `none` | `zstd` or `lz4`: the **whole batch** is compressed, stored compressed and sent compressed to consumers, so bigger batches compress better |
| `acks` | `all` | keep it |
`ProduceAsync` completes when the batch holding the record is acknowledged, so awaiting each call one by one in a
loop sends one record per round trip. For throughput, start many and await them together, or use `Produce` with a
delivery handler, and call `producer.Flush(timeout)` before shutting down so nothing is left in the accumulator.

steps.prompt: Ten records for one partition arrive 2 ms apart. A batch holds 4 records and `linger.ms` is 5. What does this print?
code: if (batch.Count > 0 && now - opened >= lingerMs) { requests++; batch.Clear(); }
explain: Every batch is opened, gets two more records in the next 4 ms, and is sent when the third record would arrive 6 ms
after it opened: linger wins every time and batches of 3 go out (0-2, 3-5, 6-8), then the last record alone. Ten
records in four requests instead of ten. A longer `linger.ms` would fill batches of 4.

steps.title: A record accumulator
prompt: Write a class `Accumulator` that batches records per partition the way the producer does.
- `string? Add(int partition, string record, long nowMs)`: adds the record to that partition's open batch (opening
one, stamped with `nowMs`, if there is none). If the batch now holds `batchSize` records it is sent at once: remove it
and return it as `"P{partition}[{records joined with ','}]"`. Otherwise return `null`.
- `List<string> Drain(long nowMs)`: removes and returns every open batch that has lingered long enough
(`nowMs - opened >= lingerMs`), in ascending partition order.
- `List<string> Flush()`: removes and returns **every** open batch, in ascending partition order (what
starter: public string? Add(int partition, string record, long nowMs) => null;
solution: readonly SortedDictionary<int, (long Opened, List<string> Records)> open = new();
static string Format(int partition, List<string> records) => $"P{partition}[{string.Join(",", records)}]";
public string? Add(int partition, string record, long nowMs)
var ready = open.Where(kv => nowMs - kv.Value.Opened >= lingerMs).Select(kv => kv.Key).ToList();
hints: A `SortedDictionary<int, (long Opened, List<string> Records)>` keeps partitions in order for you.
In `Drain`, collect the ready partitions first, then remove them (you cannot remove while enumerating).
template: var dojoA = new Accumulator(3, 5);
Dojo.Check("a record opens a batch and waits", dojoA.Add(0, "a", 0) is null, "Add should return null until the batch is full");
dojoA.Add(1, "x", 1);
dojoA.Add(0, "b", 2);
Dojo.Eq("a full batch is sent at once", "P0[a,b,c]", dojoA.Add(0, "c", 3));
Dojo.Eq("nothing has lingered long enough at t=4", new List<string>(), dojoA.Drain(4));
Dojo.Eq("P1 goes once linger.ms has passed", new List<string> { "P1[x]" }, dojoA.Drain(6));
dojoA.Add(2, "m", 10);
dojoA.Add(0, "d", 11);
Dojo.Eq("drain returns batches in partition order", new List<string> { "P0[d]", "P2[m]" }, dojoA.Drain(20));
dojoA.Add(1, "y", 30);
dojoA.Add(3, "z", 31);
Dojo.Eq("Flush sends whatever is open", new List<string> { "P1[y]", "P3[z]" }, dojoA.Flush());
Dojo.Eq("after Flush nothing is left", new List<string>(), dojoA.Drain(1000));

steps.title: Retries make duplicates; idempotence removes them
body: A producer retries failed sends (`retries` is effectively unlimited, bounded by `delivery.timeout.ms`, which is
120 s in Java; librdkafka calls it `message.timeout.ms`, 300 s). The dangerous failure is the **lost answer**:
```text
producer --- batch [A2] ---> leader writes A2 at offset 1180
producer <--- response lost (timeout, connection reset)
producer --- retry  [A2] ---> leader writes A2 AGAIN at offset 1181      without idempotence
The **idempotent producer** fixes this inside Kafka. The producer gets a **producer id (PID)** and numbers every batch
per partition with a **sequence number**. The leader remembers the last sequences per PID and partition (the last 5
batches), so a retry of a sequence it already wrote is answered "ok" **without appending**, and a sequence that skips
ahead is rejected with `OUT_OF_ORDER_SEQUENCE`.
- It requires `acks=all`, retries, and at most 5 requests in flight per connection, which is also what keeps order
during retries (next module).
- **Confluent.Kafka / librdkafka defaults `enable.idempotence` to false.** The Java client defaults it to true since
Kafka 3.0. In .NET always set `EnableIdempotence = true`.
- It covers retries **inside one producer session**. A restarted service gets a new PID, and your own code resending
after a crash is a new record: for that you need transactions or an idempotent consumer.
Exactly-once read-process-write uses **transactions**: `TransactionalId`, `producer.InitTransactions(t)`,
`BeginTransaction()`, produce, `SendOffsetsToTransaction(offsets, consumer.ConsumerGroupMetadata, t)`,
`CommitTransaction()`; downstream consumers set `IsolationLevel = IsolationLevel.ReadCommitted`.
> **See it:** in **Labs → Messaging builder → Kafka**, play *Duplicates from retries*.

steps.prompt: orders-api uses Confluent.Kafka with `Acks = Acks.All` and no other delivery settings. A network blip loses the broker's answer to a batch that was written. What can the topic end up with?
options: The same order twice: `EnableIdempotence` defaults to false in librdkafka, so the retry is appended again
No copy: the write is rolled back when the answer is lost
An exception and no retry: retries are off by default
explain: `acks` is about **durability**, not duplicates. Retries are on by default, so a lost answer leads to a second copy
unless the broker can recognise the retry, which is exactly what the PID and sequence numbers of

steps.prompt: Put the idempotent retry in the order it happens.
lines: The producer (PID 42) sends batch seq 7 for orders-0
The leader appends it at offset 1180 and the ISR copies it
The response is lost and the request times out
The producer retries the same batch, still seq 7
The leader sees seq 7 was already written for PID 42 on orders-0
The leader answers success with offset 1180 and appends nothing
explain: The retry carries the **same** sequence number, which is how the leader tells a retry from a new record. A new
record from the same producer would carry seq 8.

code: using var producer = new ProducerBuilder<string, string>(pc).Build();
var r = await producer.__4__("orders", new Message<string, string> { Key = orderId, Value = json });
explain: `EnableIdempotence = true` (not the librdkafka default), a slightly longer linger for fuller batches, zstd for
compression. `ProduceAsync` returns a `DeliveryResult` with `Partition`, `Offset` and `TopicPartitionOffset`, and
throws `ProduceException<TKey, TValue>` when delivery fails for good.

steps.title: The leader's duplicate check
prompt: Write the check the partition leader runs for the idempotent producer.
- `List<string> Records` (get): the records in the log, in offset order.
- `string Append(long producerId, int sequence, string value)`:
- for a producer id seen for the first time, the expected sequence is `0`; afterwards it is the last written
- `sequence` equal to the expected one: append, return `"appended at {offset}"`;
- `sequence` lower than expected (a retry): do **not** append, return `"duplicate of {offset}"`, the offset where that
- `sequence` higher than expected: do not append, return `"OUT_OF_ORDER_SEQUENCE (expected {expected})"`.
starter: public string Append(long producerId, int sequence, string value)
solution: public string Append(long producerId, int sequence, string value)
hints: Per producer id keep the list of offsets its sequences were written at: its `Count` is the expected next sequence.
Compare `sequence` with `written.Count`: lower is a duplicate (`written[sequence]`), higher is a gap.
template: var dojoL = new IdempotentLog();
Dojo.Eq("first batch", "appended at 0", dojoL.Append(42, 0, "A1"));
Dojo.Eq("next sequence", "appended at 1", dojoL.Append(42, 1, "A2"));
Dojo.Eq("a retry after a lost answer is not written again", "duplicate of 1", dojoL.Append(42, 1, "A2"));
Dojo.Eq("another producer has its own sequences", "appended at 2", dojoL.Append(7, 0, "B1"));
Dojo.Eq("a gap is rejected", "OUT_OF_ORDER_SEQUENCE (expected 2)", dojoL.Append(42, 3, "A4"));
Dojo.Eq("the missing batch arrives", "appended at 3", dojoL.Append(42, 2, "A3"));
Dojo.Eq("then the retried later batch fits", "appended at 4", dojoL.Append(42, 3, "A4"));
Dojo.Eq("an old retry still points at its offset", "duplicate of 0", dojoL.Append(42, 0, "A1"));
Dojo.Eq("a restarted service gets a new PID, so its resend is a new record", "appended at 5", dojoL.Append(43, 0, "A4"));
Dojo.Eq("a new PID must start at sequence 0", "OUT_OF_ORDER_SEQUENCE (expected 0)", dojoL.Append(44, 5, "x"));
Dojo.Eq("the log has one copy per accepted batch", new List<string> { "A1", "A2", "B1", "A3", "A4", "A4" }, dojoL.Records);
